Quick summary of findings from initial triage:
- Root cause: interaction between v5.1 attention kernel and q8v2 quant profile when sequence lengths exceed ~512 tokens. We see repeated per-token stall events where the GPU kernel falls back to a slower path and triggers memory re-syncs; this produces latency amplification and occasional watchdog-triggered process restarts (manifesting as 5xx).
- Why BrightLeaf: their workload median seq ~= 680 and high concurrency; this pushes the runtime into a memory-pressure regime we didn't fully cover in our q8v2 stress tests.

Immediate remediation options:
A) Tenant pin rollback: pin BrightLeaf to v5.0 + q-default for their tenant only. Time: ~45–75 minutes to coordinate across region and drain connections. Risk: low; requires config flip and small restart of serving instances for that tenant.
B) Global rollback of v5.1: ~2–3 hours with higher blast radius; avoids per-tenant config but impacts other customers.
C) Hotfix: tweak kernel fallback threshold and disable the problematic fallback; engineering estimate 6–12 hours for a safe release + canary.

My recommendation: perform tenant pin rollback now (A) and open a P0 Jira (INF-5983) to track full root-cause + longer-term fix. If customer requests global rollback we can escalate but prefer tenant pin to limit collateral.

I'm starting the pin rollback runbook now: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-5983
